summary.headline: Indo Rama Synthetics Q2 FY27 PAT rose 201.8% YoY to INR74.1 crore on EBITDA margin of 8.8%, with a fresh INR200 crore specialty expansion approved.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 total income rose 10% YoY to INR1,344 crore and EBITDA rose 46.4% to INR117.7 crore, with margin up 220 bps to 8.8%. H1 total income fell 9.7% to INR2,284 crore on supply chain issues, yet H1 EBITDA rose 24.9% to INR225.7 crore at a 9.9% margin. Net debt fell to about INR852 crore from INR1,113 crore at FY26-end, and H1 operating cash flow was INR328.5 crore. The board approved about INR200 crore of specialty filament and fibre capacity at Butibori, with commercial operations expected in calendar 2027.

segments.name: Polyester staple fibre (PSF) and filament yarn (POY/FDY)
segments.commentary: Management said these lines are running at about 100% utilisation. Yarn realisations were cited at roughly INR125-160 per kg across grades.

segments.name: PET chips / bottle-grade PET resin
segments.commentary: Chip plant is running at about 60% of capacity, which management cited as the main reason volumes are lower. Bottle-grade PET resin capacity is 2.28 lakh tonnes per annum.

segments.name: Draw textured yarn (DTY), via subsidiary
segments.commentary: Installed DTY capacity is 1.75 lakh tonnes per annum after 39 machines were added in 2023. Management said DTY's share of the mix stays at 30-35% and textured yarn margins are not currently above average.

guidance_outlook: Management expects H2 margins to hold near the 9.9% H1 level and sees a path to double-digit EBITDA margins in FY28-29.

FY27 volume expected at about 4 lakh tonnes versus about 4.75 lakh tonnes in FY26, with a return to 4.75 lakh tonnes-plus in FY28; management said FY27 turnover should still exceed FY26's roughly INR5,000 crore.

Specialty expansion (INR200 crore) expected to add about 15% to top line and 20% to EBITDA, with payback under 2 years, subject to execution. Management said about INR100 crore of incremental EBITDA would come in FY28-29.
FY27 EBITDA expected to exceed INR400 crore, implying a strong H2 versus H1's INR225.7 crore.
capex_capacity: Current capacity is 6.72 lakh tonnes per annum: 2.31 lakh tonnes PSF, 1.7 lakh tonnes DTY and 2.28 lakh tonnes bottle-grade PET resin. Polyester chip capacity was debottlenecked to 1,920 tonnes per day in February 2023.
Capacity utilisation was 58% in FY23 and 55% in FY24, then 58% in FY25 and 68% in FY26.

INR200 crore fresh investment at Butibori, across the company and wholly owned subsidiary Indorama Ventures Yarns Private Limited. It adds extruders to existing lines for specialty filament at about 115-120 tonnes per day (converting semi-dull to specialty) and another filament line of about 70 tonnes per day. A closed fibre line is being restarted for specialty and hollow fibre.
Commercial operations expected in calendar 2027, funded by term loans and internal accruals.
Growth capex was about INR20 crore in FY25 and about INR5 crore in FY26, after INR628 crore invested across FY23-FY24.
demand_pricing: Pricing is variable, linked to market prices; management said raw material costs rose 40-50% and that increases were passed through with a lag of about a week to 10 days. Raw material inventory is held for roughly 15 days to 1.5 months.
Management said spreads were about 9.9% EBITDA in H1 and expects this to be maintained for the next two quarters.

Export share fell to about 6% in the last six months from 20-25% earlier, as domestic demand was more lucrative. Management said exports could return to 20-25% after the India-UK and India-EU trade agreements.
Management said Chinese competition has eased because of yuan depreciation (INR12 to INR14.5 per yuan since early 2025) and China exiting commodity business.
Recycled bottle-to-bottle chip was INR8-10 per kg above virgin chip at the start of the year. Virgin chip prices have since risen INR30-40 per kg, so recycled chip is now cheaper, per management.

Management said India imports about 2.5 million tonnes of PTA. New domestic PTA capacity from IOCL at Paradip (1.2 million tonnes), GAIL at Mangalore (1.25 million tonnes), and Reliance is expected in 2027-28. Management expects a 2-3% sourcing gain from this.

qa_highlights.question: What are current spreads and will they hold for the next quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 EBITDA margin was 9.9% and it expects this to be maintained for the next two quarters, with no big change seen.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume and revenue outlook, and what limits utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 volume is about 4 lakh tonnes versus 4.75 lakh tonnes in FY26, recovering to 4.75 lakh tonnes-plus in FY28. The PET chip plant is at about 60% while PSF and POY run at 100%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR200 crore project add about INR100 crore of EBITDA per year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 EBITDA will be above INR400 crore and the INR100 crore uplift from the project will come in FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company expand polyester capacity given PTA availability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will decide next year once PTA capacity is up and Middle East and oil prices settle, and that a clearer picture will follow then.

qa_highlights.question: Will DTY's share of the mix change, and is the new output for captive use or the market?
qa_highlights.answer: DTY stays at the same share. The new specialty yarn and fibre output is for the market, not captive use.

qa_highlights.question: What is the specialty project's technology and capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Extruders are being added to existing lines to make cationic, dope-dyed and coloured filament, at about 115-120 tonnes per day plus about 70 tonnes per day on separate machines. A closed fibre line will restart for specialty and hollow fibre.

qa_highlights.question: How do proposed duty changes on POY, FDY and textured yarn affect pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not see a change. Its PTA and fibre inputs carry 5% duty, so duty cuts would be neutral to positive, and it has asked for an increase from 5% to 10%.

qa_highlights.question: Will new PTA plants change sourcing and freight costs for the Nagpur plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Central India location disadvantage versus Gujarat should narrow as Odisha and Mangalore plants come on stream, though the size of the freight saving is not yet known.

qa_highlights.question: Can double-digit EBITDA margins be sustained in FY28-29, and how soon can new polyester capacity arrive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will target double digits from 9.9%. It said new greenfield polyester capacity would take 3-4 years, not before 2030, because no capacity is currently in the pipeline.

risks_watch: West Asia geopolitical disruption: Strait of Hormuz shipping routes are affecting raw material availability, freight and insurance costs. Crude is at about USD115 per barrel per management.
Margin durability: management expects raw material prices to fall later, which could reduce pass-through pricing; it has not quantified the effect.
Execution on the INR200 crore specialty project (commissioning in calendar 2027) and on the ramp-up of the PET chip plant from 60% utilisation.
Timing of new domestic PTA capacity (IOCL Paradip, GAIL Mangalore, Reliance) in 2027-28, and whether freight and sourcing savings materialise.
Management said Q1 FY27 was weak, and H1 total income fell 9.7%, so H2 needs a sharp step-up to deliver the stated FY27 EBITDA above INR400 crore.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and cash generation, with management saying it targets double-digit EBITDA margins. It was more cautious on volume recovery, expansion timing and PTA-driven sourcing benefits, which it tied to the Middle East and oil-price outlook.
key_quotes: Now, as the cost optimization has been done and the plant is running quite well and that's why we are taking this INR200 crores further investment
Definitely from 9.9%, definitely we'll target on double digits. It should not go down, we are going to.
Not less than 3 years to 4 years, because environment nowadays is very important.
Unless the double -digit margins will be there, nobody is going to invest. So margin has to go up for new investment to come.
